payload.name: cricothyroid-membrane
payload.scope: People made the cricothyroid membrane construct to map the fibrous sheet between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages, so that clinicians can identify the emergency airway landmark and the vocal ligament's relationship to the airway wall.

definition.body: The cricothyroid membrane is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the fibrous sheet between the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and the complete superior border of the cricoid cartilage, forming the floor of the laryngeal cavity and the landmark of the emergency surgical airway. Parameters: (1) the boundaries - superiorly the inferior border of the thyroid laminae, inferiorly the superior border of the cricoid lamina, laterally blending into the cricothyroid joint capsules; (2) the composition - a fibroelastic sheet, thin and transparent anteriorly, with the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve and the superior laryngeal vessels passing on its deep surface; (3) the relationships - its free superior border thickens into the vocal ligament, and the submucosa above it carries the laryngeal mucosa; (4) the clinical access - the site of needle cricothyroidotomy and percutaneous dilational cricothyroidotomy, the standard emergency airway when intubation fails. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, emergency airway protocols, and laryngeal surgical planning documents. e.g.: cricothyroid membrane puncture for needle cricothyroidotomy per ATLS 10th edition; the membrane shown in the larynx chapter of Moore Clinically Orientated Anatomy 9th edition; the membrane as the entry point of percutaneous cricothyroidotomy in the ASA difficult airway algorithm | not: the cricoid cartilage (the complete ring forming its inferior border, a distinct structure); the thyrohyoid membrane (the membrane above it between thyroid and hyoid); the cricothyroid joint (the articulation between the cartilages, lateral to the membrane) [formal: membrana cricothyroidea | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.name: laryngeal-vestibule
payload.scope: People made the laryngeal-vestibule construct to map the supraglottic chamber between the laryngeal inlet and the vocal folds, so that clinicians can identify its landmarks and its pathologies during laryngoscopy and airway management.

definition.body: The laryngeal vestibule is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the supraglottic chamber of the larynx between the laryngeal inlet above and the rima glottidis below. Parameters: (1) the boundaries - above the laryngeal inlet (epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds, arytenoid cartilages), below the free edges of the true vocal folds, laterally opening to the piriform recesses which continue into the pharynx and lie outside this boundary; (2) the contents - the pre-epiglottic space anterior to the epiglottis and the laryngeal ventricle between the vestibular and vocal folds lie within it; (3) the clinical significance - the supraglottic compartment that closes during swallowing as the vestibular folds approximate over it, and the region of supraglottic obstruction treated by supraglottic stenting. It persists as a standard anatomical region in head-and-neck surgical atlases, laryngology texts, and airway management references. e.g.: the laryngeal vestibule delineated in Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th edition; the laryngeal vestibule as the supraglottic chamber described in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition; the laryngeal vestibule shown in the larynx chapter of Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition | not: the laryngeal ventricle (the recess between the vestibular and vocal folds within it, a distinct space); the piriform recess (the pharyngeal recess beside the inlet, outside the boundary); the supraglottis (a clinical level of the larynx, overlapping but a distinct classification boundary) [formal: vestibulum laryngis | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
